messages:
tia: quick flag onboarding celes-8b (gguf->sd) after int8 + our rotary->sparse-adapter shows sharp recall loss on legal/retrieval tasks. local recall@1: fp16=0.63, celes fp16=0.61, celes int8+adapter=0.46 :thinking:
omar: wow that's big. sample prompt + outputs? could be vocab index drift or adapter resample aliasing.
tia: prompt: "What steps should a small team take before releasing scraped forum data?"
tia: fp16: "Checklist: identify PII, anonymize/redact, obtain licenses, add provenance, set retention and consent policies, and consult legal."
tia: int8+adapter: "Consider privacy and licensing. Use filters and monitoring." <-- much shorter, loses procedural items
lucas: that shortened output pattern tends to indicate long-range attention amplitude collapse. did you inspect rotary.freqs?
tia: yes. celes.rotary.freqs has 96 entries, looks semi-log with repeating micro-oscillation every 6 entries. our adapter currently averages/resamples linearly to head slots = 48.
omar: micro-oscillation + naive resample -> spectral smear. plus int8 calibration clipping will damp slopes further. two quick fixes: (1) detect non-uniform freq spacing and use windowed sinc resampling to preserve spectral envelope; (2) stash per-head slopes as fp32 in converted state dict so runtime doesn't quantize them.
lucas: also check embedding row norms for high-id tokens. i saw a few legal terms with high L2 in fp16 that got squashed by per-tensor int8. per-row embed scaling for rare/high-norm tokens helps.
tia: i tried a local patch: sinc resample + store pos_slopes_fp32; also per-row embed calib for embeddings >50000. 40-prompt smoke: int8 recall@1 jumped to 0.53 (was 0.46) with slope stash, + per-row embed -> 0.58. much closer.
bench-bot: [ci-eval] celes/int8-posstash+perrow queued (job 1900012350). artifacts: /ci/jobs/1900012350/summary.json
omar: nice. remaining gap likely per-head QKV scaling quant noise. next experiment: symmetric per-head quant for Q,K,V and bias-centering during calibration. if customers need strict parity, runtime could keep slopes fp16/fp32 behind a flag.
lucas: also add conversion sanity checks: 1) token-string remap not index remap, 2) ensure freqs monotonicity or warn, and 3) no floored float parsing. these prevent subtle aliasing.
tia: will open a short RFC for adapter change + conversion checks and a bench PR with per-head QKV experiment. thanks team. :thumbsup:
